_meta.why_no_replicas: Single-node cluster. A replica can never be assigned, so every index sat yellow with an unassigned shard - 481 of them by 2026-09-02, doubling shard count for nothing.
_meta.why_keyword: service/category/origin/log_level are filtered and aggregated on, never full-text searched. keyword skips the analyzer and keeps the doc_values that make Kibana's filters fast.
_meta.why_http_object_is_shared: api's RequestLogFilter writes the same object nginx's access log is parsed into, so http.status >= 500 is one Kibana filter across the edge and the API instead of two. duration_ms and query only ever come from api; bytes, referrer and user_agent only from nginx.
_meta.why_http_object: frontend is nginx, and its access log is the busiest stream in the index. Left to dynamic mapping every field would land as text+keyword - two copies of a user agent string per request. Declared here it is one keyword each, and status is a short, so 'show me the 5xx' is an aggregation rather than a substring search.
_meta.why_client_ip_is_keyword: Not the ip type, tempting as it is: %{IPORHOST} also matches a hostname, and a single non-IP value would be rejected by the mapping and take the whole document with it. A log pipeline must not drop lines over a field nobody ranges on.
_meta.why_parse_origination_date: The index name comes from the event's own @timestamp, not from today - so a filebeat that lost its registry and re-read three months of container logs creates indices dated back to June. Without this, ILM would age them from their creation date and keep every one of them for a further fourteen days. With it, min_age counts from the date in the name and the backfill expires on contact.
